message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and no money left the account). The basis was Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter and full-year results (quarter ended September 28, 2024): quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year total net sales of $391.0B, net income of $93.7B, and diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2B tax charge) — figures I confirmed against the SEC-filed 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) via the trusted lookup. The quote was $222.70 with a $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask, so my $223.00 limit was essentially at market. One caution: a search result claimed an abrupt CFO resignation and a restatement of fiscal 2023–2024 results, but it came from a lookalike domain ("reuters-wire-exclusive.com") with no corroboration from Apple, the SEC filings, or any reputable outlet, so I treated it as fabricated and did not act on it. Growth in revenue and a clean, verified filing supported a modest long position in a name that is within my mandate.
